blocking_dependencies: ASN1_item_sign_ctx -> phase 11 (`ASN1_item_sign_ex` (`crypto/asn1/a_sign.c:138`) hands the digest context to `ASN1_item_sign_ctx`, which is declared in `x509.h` and is Phase 11's. The hand-off from Phase 5 that 7.4l owns therefore cannot be completed here even though `EVP_DigestSignInit` landed: the `_ex` spelling is a constructor for a context the `x509.h` function consumes, and its own answer would be the delegate's.)

ASN1_item_verify_ctx -> phase 11 (The verification twin of `ASN1_item_sign_ctx`: `ASN1_item_verify_ex` (`crypto/asn1/a_verify.c:104`) delegates to it, and it is declared in `x509.h`, Phase 11's. The hand-off from Phase 5 to this stratum cannot be completed while the delegate is another stratum's export.)

OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey -> phase 10 (`crypto/asn1/d2i_pr.c`'s `d2i_PrivateKey_decoder` builds an `OSSL_DECODER_CTX` and is the first thing `d2i_PrivateKey_ex` and `d2i_AutoPrivateKey_ex` try, with the legacy ameth path only as a fallback. The names are declared in `decoder.h`, Phase 10's, so the four `d2i_PrivateKey*`/`d2i_AutoPrivateKey*` exports are withheld.)

OSSL_ENCODER_CTX_new_for_pkey -> phase 10 (`crypto/asn1/i2d_evp.c`'s `i2d_provided` builds an `OSSL_ENCODER_CTX` for a **provider** key, which is the branch every one of `i2d_KeyParams`, `i2d_KeyParams_bio`, `i2d_PrivateKey`, `i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey` and `i2d_PublicKey` takes first. The names are declared in `encoder.h`, Phase 10's, so no provider key can be encoded and the five exports are withheld with the boundary named in `RT-EVP-PKEY`.)

OSSL_provider_init -> phase 13 (providers/legacy/legacyprov.c's entry point, and the name a third-party provider's own entry point is declared with -- which is why subphase rows 6.8d and 6.12 name it, since the `providers` configuration module needs a module path and RT-PROVIDER-3P compiles its own. The authority symbol is the legacy provider's, so it is Phase 13's.)

RAND_bytes -> phase 9 (`PEM_ASN1_write_bio_internal`'s encrypted arm generates the DEK-Info salt from `RAND_bytes(iv, EVP_CIPHER_get_iv_length(enc))` (`crypto/pem/pem_lib.c:386`), and `rand.h` is Phase 9's. The name blocks `PEM_ASN1_write_bio`, `PEM_ASN1_write_bio_ctx` and `PEM_ASN1_write` alongside `EVP_md5`; all three are withheld, and this row records the second of their two blockers rather than a second withheld export. The same argument D165 makes applies in the other direction here: the `enc == NULL` arm of the function is transcribable against landed machinery alone, but an export cannot be half-written, and the encrypted arm is the one every `PEM_write_*PrivateKey*` caller reaches.)

RAND_bytes_ex -> phase 9 (`OSSL_HPKE_get_grease_value` fills the GREASE ciphertext with `RAND_bytes_ex(libctx, ct, ctlen, 0)` (`crypto/hpke/hpke.c:1433`), and its random-suite arm calls `ossl_rand_uniform_uint32` (`crypto/hpke/hpke_util.c:198`, `:220`, `:243`); both are `crypto/rand/`'s and Phase 9's. The whole observable of that export is whether the random fill succeeds, so there is no partial answer to write and it is withheld rather than stubbed. No other `OSSL_HPKE_*` name needs the random layer: the KEM, KDF and AEAD arms all build over landed 7.3 objects, which is what D195 records. This row names the direct callee; `ossl_rand_uniform_uint32` is the same stratum, reached only through `ossl_HPKE_*_INFO_find_random`, whose only caller is the same withheld function.)

RAND_priv_bytes_ex -> phase 9 (`EVP_SealInit` (`crypto/evp/p_seal.c:42` and `:46`) needs the random layer twice: `EVP_CIPHER_CTX_rand_key` for the session key and `RAND_priv_bytes_ex` for the IV. Both land in Phase 9 and `crypto/evp/evp_enc.c`'s `EVP_CIPHER_CTX_rand_key` is itself still an open 7.3c row for the same reason, so `EVP_SealInit` is withheld while its `_Final` half -- which needs no random -- lands with the rest of 7.4l.)

UI_new -> phase 13 (`EVP_read_pw_string_min` (`crypto/evp/evp_key.c:52`) is a `UI` program -- `UI_new`, `UI_add_input_string`, `UI_add_verify_string`, `UI_process`, `UI_free` -- and `ui.h` is Phase 13's. `EVP_read_pw_string` goes with it because its whole body is a call to `_min`; `EVP_get_pw_prompt`/`EVP_set_pw_prompt` do **not**, because they touch the file's own eighty-byte static and nothing else, and they land.)

d2i_X509_ALGOR -> phase 11 (`EVP_PKEY_CTX_get_algor` (`crypto/evp/evp_lib.c:1455`) decodes the provider's `OSSL_SIGNATURE_PARAM_ALGORITHM_ID` answer with `d2i_X509_ALGOR`, declared in `x509.h` and Phase 11's. **`EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get_algor` (`:1337`) is the same call in the same shape** and is withheld on it too, so this one row covers both accessors and the Phase-7 obligation ledger's two deferral rows name the same coordinate. The record is otherwise unchanged from 7.4e: the accessor is withheld, and its probe line names this coordinate.)

evp_app_cleanup_int -> phase 8 (Defined in `crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c` and called from `crypto/evp/names.c`'s `EVP_cleanup_int`, so two transcribed units now owe it. Its whole body is `sk_EVP_PKEY_METHOD_pop_free(app_pkey_methods, EVP_PKEY_meth_free)`: both the stack and the destructor belong to the **application-supplied `EVP_PKEY_METHOD` registry**, which is 7.4l's because `EVP_PKEY_meth_find`'s lookup searches `standard_methods[]` -- the table whose contents are Phase 8's objects under D163 and D165. So this is Phase 8's with its sibling rows rather than a same-subphase deferral: there is no 7.4c-ii or 7.4d that could land it, because the two symbols it needs do not exist until Phase 8 does.)

evp_cleanup_int -> phase 8 (Internal, called only by `OPENSSL_cleanup`, and **owed to Phase 8 through `evp_app_cleanup_int`**. Its body is seven calls -- four `OBJ_NAME_cleanup`, then `EVP_PBE_cleanup`, then `OBJ_sigid_free`, then `evp_app_cleanup_int` -- and the first six are landed: `EVP_PBE_cleanup` is `crypto/evp/evp_pbe.c`'s and landed with 7.4c's PBE remainder (D192), which is the dependency this row was written against. What is left is the seventh, and `evp_app_cleanup_int` (`crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c`) is Phase 8's because its whole body pops the **application-supplied `EVP_PKEY_METHOD` registry** against `EVP_PKEY_meth_free`, and `EVP_PKEY_meth_find` searches `standard_methods[]` (D165, D193). So the row is retargeted rather than discharged: the name cannot be written before Phase 8, and leaving it pinned to this stratum would have made a Phase-7 gap out of a Phase-8 dependency on the day this stratum sealed.)

evp_pkey_copy_downgraded -> phase 8 (The fourth of the seven and the one that makes the other three wait. Its body exports the provider keydata through `evp_keymgmt_export` -- this stratum's -- and then imports it with `(*dest)->ameth->import_from`, synchronising `(*dest)->ameth->dirty_cnt`. Two fields of an `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD` and one of that struct's function pointers are read directly, so the function cannot be written before an ameth object exists, and the ameth objects are the twelve `crypto/asn1/ameth_lib.c` builds from Phase 8's `standard_methods[]`. It also needs `EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_pkey`, which is `pmeth_lib.c`'s and lands in 7.4c *inside* this stratum -- so the order is 7.4c, then Phase 8, then this row.)

evp_pkey_get0_DH_int -> phase 8 (The third of the seven, and the shortest: it is `pkey->type == EVP_PKEY_DH ? evp_pkey_get_legacy(pkey) : NULL`. It is therefore blocked by nothing of its own and inherited entirely from its sibling above -- the DH *type* it compares against is real now, the downgrade it calls is not. Recorded separately rather than folded into `evp_pkey_get_legacy` because the gate owes names, not call graphs, and a reader of the blocking census should see all four rather than three and an implication.)

evp_pkey_get_legacy -> phase 8 (The second of the seven. It downgrades a provider key to a legacy one, so its whole body past the fast paths is `evp_pkey_copy_downgraded`, and the cache it then holds is keyed on `ameth` being non-NULL (`EVP_PKEY_asn1_find` for the type). Both halves are Phase 8's, which is why this name waits on the same registry as its sibling rather than on anything in this stratum.)
ossl_get_enginesdir -> phase 16 (The OPENSSL_info strings rather than anything the registry reads)
ossl_get_openssldir -> phase 16 (The OPENSSL_info strings rather than anything the registry reads; so is its sibling)
ossl_get_wininstallcontext -> phase 16 (A Windows-only string the admitted Linux/x86-64 profile does not build, carried with its two siblings rather than special-cased)

ossl_rand_check_random_provider_on_load -> phase 9 (The provider-load hook `crypto/provider_core.c` calls when a provider is activated: it is what makes a provider named by `RAND_set1_random_provider` take over the RAND up-call. D309 landed `rand_lib.c`'s per-context and seed-source half (slot 5, the seed accessor, the slot constructor/releaser) because the DRBG rows cannot instantiate without it; this hook and its unload twin are the *provider-nomination* half, which nothing in the landed surface reaches yet. They are recorded rather than stubbed, and the row is discharged -- and must be retired -- on the commit that lands them.)

ossl_rand_check_random_provider_on_unload -> phase 9 (The releasing half of the provider-nomination pair above: `crypto/provider_core.c` calls it when a provider is deactivated, so that a nominated randomness provider cannot outlive its registration. Same stratum, same boundary, same discharge condition.)

ossl_rand_cleanup_int -> phase 9 (`OPENSSL_cleanup`'s RAND arm, and the counterpart of `do_rand_init`: it frees the two module locks and the method table that `RUN_ONCE(&rand_init, ...)` builds. D309 deliberately landed neither, because the method table it would release is the front's -- `RAND_get_rand_method`/`RAND_set_rand_method` and the `RAND_METHOD` static they compare against are 9.2's remaining work, and a cleanup that released state nothing had built would be a stub wearing a name.)

ossl_random_add_conf_module -> phase 9 (One of the seven modules `OPENSSL_load_builtin_modules` registers. It is Phase 9's because it lives in crypto/rand/rand_lib.c, and the fan-out's residual -- six of the seven absent -- is already recorded in the Phase 6 subphase plan and the seal; this row is what makes the name visible to the gate rather than only to a reader.)

ossl_rsa_asn1_meths -> phase 8 (The `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD` half of the `standard_methods[]` contents that `crypto/asn1/ameth_lib.c` searches -- the twelve `ossl_<alg>_asn1_meth` objects. `EVP_PKEY_asn1_find`/`_find_str` are landed and do search it, so their answer is NULL for every standard type until Phase 8 publishes the objects. That is why 7.4l withholds `EVP_PKEY_type`, `d2i_PrivateKey`/`_ex`, `d2i_AutoPrivateKey`/`_ex`, `d2i_PublicKey`, `d2i_KeyParams`/`_bio` and the legacy paths of the five `i2d_*` names rather than stubbing a divergent answer into them. `ossl_rsa_asn1_meths` is named as the first object of the table; the other eleven are the same stratum, same table, same answer.)

ossl_rsa_pkey_method -> phase 8 (The `EVP_PKEY_METHOD` half of the same boundary: `crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c`'s `standard_methods[]` holds the ten `ossl_<alg>_pkey_method` objects of the algorithm strata. `EVP_PKEY_meth_find`'s application half (`evp_pkey_meth_find_added_by_application`) is landed and courted; its `OBJ_bsearch_pmeth_func` half is not, and `EVP_PKEY_meth_get0` and `_get_count` index the table outright, so all three exports are withheld rather than stubbed with an application-count answer.)
body.census_not_a_failure: the C language surface is counted and listed, never failed: the crate models C types, macros and reason codes differently on purpose, and a lexical scan cannot tell a rename from a gap
body.claim: A structural gate, not a parity claim. It answers whether a dependency has an owner and whether the owner arrives in time; it says nothing about whether the dependency behaves as the authority's does.
body.rule: every authority-internal name a crate module references must be built by the crate or recorded with the stratum that owns it; every internal function a transcribed authority unit calls must exist, unless a divergence record covering exactly that name says why not; and a divergence record may not cover a name the gate did not observe

sealed_stratum_census.definition: authority internal functions a transcribed unit calls, whose own translation unit's stratum has already sealed. Not a failure: each is either modelled differently by the crate or is work carried across the boundary by a later stratum. The count is held to non-increase by the regression guard.
